sections.name: Sake List
items: Less sweet and more citrusy sake infused with fresh yuzu juice. Pairs with spicy flavors.
Dry, clean, light bodied, well balanced with notes of hazelnut and toasted rice. Considered an everyday sake. Pairs with most foods.
Floral nose, smooth, juicy and refreshing, with notes of tropical fruit offset by star anise and a soft finish. Pairs with Richer flavors like seafood, vegetables, and Caesar salads.

Bright tart flavor of plum. Aromas of apricot and cinnamon, medium bodied with notes of wild strawberries and a tart finish. A beautifully restrained and elegant umeshu (plum sake). Pairs with sweeter flavors.
Smooth and refreshing, aromas of honey and sugarcane, layered with roasted almonds. Subtle hints of pear, grapefruit, and dark chocolate. Pairs with ramen and chicken.
Pleasant balance of crisp Ginjo sake with hints of dryness and fresh lightly sweet pear and a smooth flavorful finish. Pairs with spicy broth and noodles.
Unfiltered sake with aromas of lily flowers, cantaloupes, smooth and silky texture, flavors of Muscat grape and strawberries, off dry with touch of sweetness. Pairs with spicy food, BBQ and curry

A gentle subtle sake, notes of citrus and steamed rice. Off dryness with subtle sweetness and crisp clean finish. Inspired by local yeti lore; some proceeds go to rescue efforts in local mountains. Pairs well with tofu and edamame.
Sayuri means little lily, thus a soft floral nigori with notes of white grape and cherry blossom. Pairs with spicy food, ramen, stir fry and dessert.
